==English==
{{wp}}

===Alternative forms===
* {{alt|en|s**t|sl*t||censored}}

===Etymology===
From {{inh|en|enm|slutt}}, {{m|enm|slutte}}, {{m|enm|slute|t=a dirty or slovenly person, usually a woman, scullery maid; messy animal to prepare as food; slush, mud}}, probably from {{inh|en|ang|*slȳte|t=sleet}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*slautijā}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*slautijǭ|t=sleet, hail}}, related to {{cog|gmw-pro|*slaut|t=puddle, ditch}}. Compare {{cog|nl|slodder}} and {{m|nl|slet}}, dialectal {{cog|sv|slata||idle woman}}, {{cog|no|sludd||sleet}}, and the dialectal {{cog|no|slutr||sleet, impure liquid}}. {{doublet|en|sleet}}. {{rfv-etym|en}}

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/slʌt/}}
* {{audio|en|En-US-slut.wav|a=US}}
* {{audio|en|En-au-slut.ogg|a=AU}}
* {{rhymes|en|ʌt|s=1}}
* {{IPA|en|/slʊt/|a=Northern England}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈsɫɐt/|a=AU}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# {{senseid|en|woman}} {{lb|en|vulgar|often|_|derogatory}} A [[sexual]]ly [[promiscuous]] [[woman]].
#: {{coi|en|dirty '''slut'''}}
#: {{coi|en|total '''slut'''}}
## {{senseid|en|prostitute}} {{lb|en|vulgar|by extension}} A [[prostitute]].
##: {{ux|en|You could hire a '''slut''' for a few hours, if you're that desperate.}}
# {{senseid|en|any person}} {{lb|en|vulgar|often|derogatory}} Any sexually promiscuous person.
# {{senseid|en|attention seeker}}  {{lb|en|figurative|vulgar|often|derogatory}} Someone who seeks [[attention]] through [[inappropriate]] means or to an [[excessive]] degree.
#: {{coi|en|a press '''slut'''}}
# {{senseid|en|disloyal person}} {{lb|en|vulgar|figuratively|often|derogatory}} A [[disloyal]] individual; someone who does not [[commit]] to a particular thing.
#: {{ux|en|That guy was a job '''slut'''; he changed jobs way too often and quickly, to the point that employers will no longer hire him.}}
# {{senseid|en|untidy person}} {{lb|en|archaic|derogatory}} A [[slovenly]], [[untidy]] [[person]], usually a [[woman]].
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare As You Like It|text=''Clo.'' Truly, and to cast away honestie vppon a foule '''slut''', were to put good meate into an vncleane dish. / Aud. I am not a '''slut''', though I thanke the Goddes I am foule.}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Merry Wives|text=Where fires thou find’st unrak’d, and hearths unswept, / There pinch the Maids as blew as Bill-berry, / Our radiant Queene, hates '''Sluts''', and Sluttery.}}
#* {{RQ:Bunyan Pilgrim's Progress|passage=Some cry out against sin even as the mother cries out against her child in her lap, when she calleth it '''slut''' and naughty girl, and then falls to hugging and kissing it.}}
#* '''1685''', {{w|John Dryden}}, ''Slyvae: or, the Second Part of Poetical Miscellanies'', "Lucretius: The Fourth Book. Concerning the Nature of Love,: lines 142-46:
# {{senseid|en|bold woman}} {{lb|en|obsolete|derogatory}} A [[bold]], outspoken woman.
#* {{RQ:John Gay Beggar's Opera|passage=Our Polly is a sad '''Slut'''! nor heeds what we have taught her.}}
#* {{RQ:Le Fanu House|volume=I|page=203|passage=To hear her rant, one would have supposed, who had not seen him, that her lank-haired, grimly partner was the prettiest youth in the county of Dublin, and that all the comely lasses in Chapelizod and the country round were sighing and setting caps at him; and Devereux, who had a vein of satire, and loved even farce, enjoyed the heroics of the fat old '''slut'''.}}
#* {{RQ:Shaw Pygmalion|page=190|passage=You damned impudent '''slut''', you! But it's better than snivelling; better than fetching slippers and finding spectacles, isnt it? [''Rising''] By George, Eliza, I said I'd make a woman of you; and I have. I like you like this.}}
# {{senseid|en|dog}} {{lb|en|obsolete}} A [[female]] [[dog]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1852|author=Susanna Moodie|title=w:Roughing it in the Bush|url=https://www.gutenberg.ca/ebooks/moodie-roughingit1871/moodie-roughingit1871-00-h-dir/moodie-roughingit1871-00-h.html|text=‘Bête!’ returned the angry Frenchman, bestowing a savage kick on one of the unoffending pups which was frisking about his feet. The pup yelped; the '''slut''' barked and leaped furiously at the offender, and was only kept from biting him by Sam, who could scarcely hold her back for laughing; the captain was uproarious; the offended Frenchman alone maintained a severe and dignified aspect.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1982|author={{w|Paul Radley}}|title=My Blue-Checker Corker and Me|publisher=Fontana/Collins|location=Sydney|page=17|text=‘Like a '''slut''' and all the dogs mounting her.’}}
# {{senseid|en|maidservant}} {{lb|en|obsolete}} A [[maidservant]].
#* {{RQ:Pepys Diary|passage=Our little girl Susan is a most admirable '''slut''', and pleases us mightily, doing more service than both the others and deserves wages better.}}
# {{senseid|en|rag}} {{lb|en|obsolete}} A [[rag]] [[soak]]ed in a [[flammable]] [[substance]] and [[lit]] for [[illumination]].
